tokens.faq_1_question: What should I check before calling for emergency HVAC repair?
tokens.faq_1_answer: Check your circuit breaker to ensure the unit didn't trip, verify your thermostat batteries and settings, and replace a dirty air filter if airflow is blocked.
tokens.faq_2_question: Do you charge extra for midnight or weekend emergency calls?
tokens.faq_2_answer: We offer upfront, flat-rate emergency pricing so you always know the exact cost before any repair work begins, regardless of the hour.
tokens.faq_3_question: How fast can an HVAC technician arrive at my home?
tokens.faq_3_answer: During extreme weather alerts (heat waves or freezes), our average emergency on-site arrival time is between 30 and 45 minutes.
tokens.faq_4_question: Can a failing capacitor cause my air conditioner to stop blowing cold air?
tokens.faq_4_answer: Yes! A blown or weak compressor capacitor is one of the most common reasons an AC unit hums but fails to start cooling during summer heat.
tokens.faq_5_question: Are your technicians certified to handle refrigerants and gas lines?
tokens.faq_5_answer: Every ClimateGuard technician is EPA-certified for refrigerant handling and fully licensed for gas furnace and electrical repairs.
